page.layout: Two printed pages on the scan. Left page: a running head with page number 168 at the top; the main text block in one column; margin notes in the left margin (three references, two set in the margin beside the text). Right page: only the cut-off line beginnings at the scan's right edge are visible, and the page is not legible beyond them.

main_text.p: &Eudoxiam anathemati subijcit e vita excessisse affirmet: cùm tamen Eudoxiä ante Chrysostomum fato cessisse,tum ex {f}Socrate, tum {t}Sozomeno liquidò constet. Sed demùs excommunicasse,non tamen e Majestatis solio deturbauit,nō Coronam à capite, Sceptrum e manu excussit, non subditos à iuramento fidelitatis exēmit; non denique eorum personas sicarijs & parricidis exposuit; quod si fecisset & superuixisset: Chrysostomus, licèt in sua causa certè reclamasset, quod partim ex eius Commentarijs in {u}Romanos, partim etiam & planiùs ex Homilia de Dauid & Saul innotefcit: in quo [?] eloquentiæ quasi torrente auditorum animos influens itá fatur. [Vidistis tensa retia, vidistis venatorem erectum, vidistis omnes adhortantes, vt ensem in hostis pectus immergeret, nunc mihi Philosophicam animi moderationem spectá, luctum, victoriam, coronam. Spelunca campus erat, luctatus est Dauid, pugilem egit, iracundia Saul, certaminis materia, Agonothetes Deus: quin potiùs non ipsi modò aduersus seipsum erat prælium, sed aduer-Lib.6. cap.10.Lib.8. c.27.& 28.Jn c.13. [?]sus

page.notes: Left page: the margin notes are "f Lib.6. cap.10.", "t Lib.8. c.27.& 28." and "u Jn c.13." ("Jn" is doubtful, possibly "In"). The text has no further notes. Marks f, t and u correspond to "Socrate", "Sozomeno" and "Romanos" in the text. The word after "in quo" is partly covered by a dark smudge and is doubtful. "Eudoxiä" is uncertain for the final mark. The first paragraph starts at the top of the column without an indent, so it continues from the previous page. The last text line "sus" completes the hyphenated word "aduer-" and is part of the text. Right page: only the line-beginnings at the scan edge are visible; the list above gives those fragments as they appear, and the rest of that page is not legible.
